newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei seen firm, but upward momentum to slow.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei seen firm, but upward momentum to slow.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index is likely to firm on Wednesday, but large gains may be getting harder to come by, brokers said.
The weak yen against the dollar will continue to encourage buying of shares in blue-chip exporters, but the extent of the gains may be limited after recent sharp rises, they said.
On Tuesday, the key 225-share Nikkei average rose 306.03 points or 1.73 percent to end at 18,021.70. Its June futures were 390 points higher at 18,040.
"The upside above 18,000 might be limited," said Osamu Yamazaki, general manger at New Japan Securities Co Ltd.

The upward momentum for blue-chip high-technology shares is expected to slow, but buying, backed by the yen's decline against the dollar, could spill over to other lower-priced shares, such as major steel issues, Yamazaki said.
The dollar continued to surge overnight, hitting a 56-month high of 126.52 yen in Europe. The U.S. currency stood at around 126.30 yen in early Asia trade on Wednesday.
Brokers also expect the Nikkei average's downside to be limited, as some sectors, such as construction, have showed signs of recovering somewhat, brokers said.
